dedupe_keys.name: tesip railway hazard severity text benchmark

description: This repository publishes a JSON benchmark of 101 railway functional-safety hazard statements paired with injury-severity labels. The README identifies a textual hazard condition as input and three normative consequence classes as output: slight injury, serious injury and death. It provides an example with a cargo-securing failure and states that the no-injury SV0 class is excluded. The material derives from the TeSiP/SIRF guideline context for railway approval. A modeller could use the structured pairs to test a hazard-coding step in a rail risk workflow or evaluate classification errors before applying a wider safety model. These labels are expert-defined normative categories, not observed casualties or calibrated failure probabilities. The file is present in the repository, but this review did not download it, inspect all 101 rows or test class balance. The repository is marked MIT and its README repeats that licence, while original guideline redistribution rights were not independently verified. There is no established publication citation yet. Related rail-safety resources may use different severity definitions and should not be merged by label alone. Its documented coverage is the 101 selected railway safety statements, with no claim to represent all rail hazards or accident frequencies.
